content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 7
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
42 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-ʾet-his-own-house Solomon built thirteen years, and-he-finished ʾet-all his-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished his entire house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon spent thirteen years building his own palace complex before it was completed.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 2
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built ʾet-the-House-of the-Forest-of Lebanon — a-hundred cubits its-length, and-fifty cubits its-width, and-thirty cubits its-height, upon four rows-of cedar pillars, and-cedar beams upon the-pillars.

**LOGOS (formal):** He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Its length was a hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He built the Palace of the Forest of Lebanon — one hundred fifty feet long, seventy-five feet wide, and forty-five feet high — with four rows of cedar columns supporting cedar beams.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was-roofed with-cedar above upon the-chambers that were upon the-pillars — forty-five; fifteen in-a-row.

**LOGOS (formal):** And it was covered with cedar above the chambers that were upon the forty-five pillars, fifteen in a row.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** It was roofed with cedar above the beams resting on the columns — forty-five beams, fifteen per row.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** And-window-frames were in-three rows, and-window-opening opposite window-opening, three times.

**LOGOS (formal):** There were window frames in three rows, and window opposite window in three tiers.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** There were three rows of windows with frames, each one facing a corresponding window opposite.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-all the-openings and-the-doorposts were squared with-frames, and-window-opening opposite window-opening, three times.

**LOGOS (formal):** All the doorways and windows had squared frames, and window was opposite window in three tiers.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** All the doorways and windows had rectangular frames, set in matching rows of three.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-the-Hall-of-Pillars he-made — fifty cubits its-length, and-thirty cubits its-width. And-a-porch was before-them, and-pillars and-a-threshold before-them.

**LOGOS (formal):** He made the Hall of Pillars; its length was fifty cubits and its breadth thirty cubits. There was a porch in front with pillars, and a canopy before them.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He made the Hall of Pillars — seventy-five feet long and forty-five feet wide — with a covered porch in front, supported by pillars.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-his-house where he-dwelt — the-other court within the-hall — was-of-the-same workmanship. And-a-house he-made for-the-daughter-of Pharaoh — whom Solomon had-taken — like this hall.

**LOGOS (formal):** His own house where he was to dwell, in the other court back of the hall, was of like workmanship. Solomon also made a house like this hall for Pharaoh's daughter whom he had taken in marriage.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** His personal residence was set in another courtyard behind the hall, built in the same style. He also built a palace like the hall for Pharaoh's daughter, whom he had married.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** All these were-of costly stones, according-to-the-measures-of hewn-stone, sawed with-the-saw, inside and-outside, and-from the-foundation to the-coping, and-from-outside to the-great court.

**LOGOS (formal):** All these were made of costly stones, cut according to measure, sawed with saws, inside and outside, from the foundation to the coping, and from outside to the great court.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** All these structures were made of premium stone blocks, precision-cut with saws on all sides, from foundation to roofline, and from the buildings out to the great courtyard.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-the-foundation was-of costly stones, great stones — stones-of ten cubits and-stones-of eight cubits.

**LOGOS (formal):** The foundation was of costly stones, huge stones, stones of eight and ten cubits.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The foundations were of massive, expensive stone — blocks fifteen feet and twelve feet long.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 11
**EMET (literal):** And-above were costly stones, according-to-the-measures-of hewn-stone, and-cedar.

**LOGOS (formal):** And above were costly stones, cut to measure, and cedar.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Above the foundation were more cut stones and cedar beams.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-the-great court all-around — three rows-of hewn-stone and-a-row-of cedar beams. And-so for-the-inner court-of the-house-of YHWH and-for-the-porch-of the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** The great court all around had three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams, like the inner court of the house of the LORD and the vestibule of the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The great courtyard was enclosed by three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams — the same construction used for the inner court of the LORD's temple and the temple vestibule.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-the-king Solomon sent and-took Hiram from-Tyre.

**LOGOS (formal):** And King Solomon sent and brought Hiram from Tyre.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** King Solomon sent for a craftsman named Hiram from Tyre.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** He was the-son-of a-widow woman from-the-tribe-of Naphtali, and-his-father was a-man-of Tyre, a-worker-of bronze. And-he-was-filled with the-wisdom and-the-understanding and-the-knowledge to-do all work in-bronze. And-he-came to the-king Solomon and-did ʾet-all his-work.

**LOGOS (formal):** He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in bronze. And he was full of wisdom, understanding, and skill for making any work in bronze. He came to King Solomon and did all his work.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** His mother was a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a Tyrian bronzeworker. Hiram was extraordinarily gifted — filled with skill, intelligence, and expertise in all kinds of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and carried out all his commissions.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-he-fashioned ʾet-the-two pillars-of bronze — eighteen cubits the-height-of the-one pillar, and-a-cord-of twelve cubits encircled ʾet-the-second pillar.

**LOGOS (formal):** He cast two pillars of bronze. Eighteen cubits was the height of one pillar, and a line of twelve cubits measured the circumference of the second pillar.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He cast two bronze pillars, each twenty-seven feet tall, with a circumference of eighteen feet.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-two capitals he-made to-set upon the-tops-of the-pillars, cast-of bronze — five cubits the-height-of the-one capital, and-five cubits the-height-of the-second capital.

**LOGOS (formal):** He made two capitals of cast bronze to set on the tops of the pillars. The height of the one capital was five cubits, and the height of the other capital was five cubits.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He made two bronze capitals to go on top of the pillars, each seven and a half feet tall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** Nets-of network, twisted-work-of chains, for-the-capitals that were upon the-top-of the-pillars — seven for-the-one capital and-seven for-the-second capital.

**LOGOS (formal):** There were lattices of checker work with wreaths of chain work for the capitals on the tops of the pillars, seven for the one capital and seven for the other capital.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The capitals had lattice networks decorated with chain designs — seven chains for each capital.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made ʾet-the-pillars, and-two rows all-around upon the-one network to-cover ʾet-the-capitals that were upon the-top with-the-pomegranates. And-so he-did for-the-second capital.

**LOGOS (formal):** Likewise he made pomegranates in two rows all around on the one latticework to cover the capital that was on the top of the pillar, and he did the same with the other capital.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He made two rows of pomegranates around each network to cover the capitals on top of the pillars.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** And-the-capitals that were upon the-top-of the-pillars were-of lily work in-the-hall — four cubits.

**LOGOS (formal):** Now the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars in the vestibule were of lily design, four cubits.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The capitals on the pillars in the vestibule were shaped like lilies, six feet tall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 20
**EMET (literal):** And-capitals on the-two pillars, also above, close-by the-belly that was beside the-network. And-the-pomegranates were two-hundred, in-rows all-around, upon the-second capital.

**LOGOS (formal):** The capitals were on the two pillars and also above, close to the rounded projection beside the latticework. There were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around on the second capital.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** On both capitals, above and next to the rounded section by the network, were two hundred pomegranates in rows all around.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 21
**EMET (literal):** And-he-set-up ʾet-the-pillars at-the-porch-of the-temple. And-he-set-up ʾet-the-right pillar and-called its-name Jachin. And-he-set-up ʾet-the-left pillar and-called its-name Boaz.

**LOGOS (formal):** He set up the pillars at the vestibule of the temple. He set up the pillar on the right and called its name Jachin, and he set up the pillar on the left and called its name Boaz.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He erected the pillars at the entrance of the temple. The one on the right he named Jachin, and the one on the left he named Boaz.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** And-upon the-top-of the-pillars was lily work. And-the-work-of the-pillars was-finished.

**LOGOS (formal):** On the top of the pillars was lily design. Thus the work of the pillars was finished.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The tops of the pillars were shaped like lilies. And so the work on the pillars was completed.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made ʾet-the-Sea, cast — ten cubits from-its-brim to-its-brim, round all-around, and-five cubits its-height, and-a-line-of thirty cubits encircled ʾet-it all-around.

**LOGOS (formal):** Then he made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim, and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He then cast the Sea — a circular basin fifteen feet from rim to rim, seven and a half feet deep, and forty-five feet in circumference.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** And-gourds beneath its-brim all-around encircled-it — ten in-a-cubit, encircling ʾet-the-Sea all-around. The-gourds were in-two rows, cast in-its-casting.

**LOGOS (formal):** Under its brim were gourds, ten to a cubit, encircling the sea all around. The gourds were cast in two rows when it was cast.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Below the rim, two rows of gourds encircled it — ten gourds per foot and a half — cast as part of the basin.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** It-stood upon twelve oxen — three facing north, and-three facing west, and-three facing south, and-three facing east. And-the-Sea was upon-them above, and-all their-hindquarters were inward.

**LOGOS (formal):** It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their rear parts were inward.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The Sea rested on twelve bronze bulls — three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east — with all their hindquarters pointing inward.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** And-its-thickness was a-handbreadth, and-its-brim was-like the-work-of the-brim-of a-cup, a-flower-of a-lily. Two-thousand baths it-held.

**LOGOS (formal):** Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The basin was three inches thick, with a rim shaped like a cup, like a lily blossom. It held about 12,000 gallons.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made ʾet-the-ten stands-of bronze — four cubits the-length-of the-one stand, and-four cubits its-width, and-three cubits its-height.

**LOGOS (formal):** He also made the ten stands of bronze. Each stand was four cubits long, four cubits wide, and three cubits high.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He also made ten bronze stands, each six feet long, six feet wide, and four and a half feet tall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 28
**EMET (literal):** And-this was the-work-of the-stand: they-had panels, and-the-panels were between the-frames.

**LOGOS (formal):** This was the construction of the stands: they had panels, and the panels were set in the frames,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The stands were constructed with panels set between uprights.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 29
**EMET (literal):** And-on the-panels that were between the-frames were lions, oxen, and-cherubim. And-on the-frames — above and-below the-lions and-the-oxen — were wreaths-of hanging-work.

**LOGOS (formal):** and on the panels that were set in the frames were lions, oxen, and cherubim. On the frames, above and below the lions and oxen, were wreaths of beveled work.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** On the panels between the uprights were lions, bulls, and cherubim. On the uprights — above and below the lions and bulls — were wreaths of hammered work.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 31
**EMET (literal):** And-its-mouth from-within the-crown and-above was a-cubit. And-its-mouth was round like-the-work-of a-stand — a-cubit and-a-half. And-also upon its-mouth were carvings, and-their-panels were square, not round.

**LOGOS (formal):** Its opening within the crown extended upward one cubit. Its opening was round, as a pedestal is made, a cubit and a half deep. At its opening there were carvings, and its panels were square, not round.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Inside the stand, the opening was round — a pedestal rising eighteen inches above, set in a circular frame twenty-seven inches deep. The opening had engravings, and the frames were square, not round.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 32
**EMET (literal):** And-the-four wheels were beneath the-panels, and-the-axles-of the-wheels were in-the-stand. And-the-height-of the-one wheel was a-cubit and-a-half.

**LOGOS (formal):** The four wheels were underneath the panels, and the axles of the wheels were of one piece with the stands. The height of a wheel was a cubit and a half.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The four wheels were under the panels. The wheel axles were attached to the stand, and each wheel was twenty-seven inches in diameter.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** And-the-work-of the-wheels was like-the-work-of a-chariot wheel — their-axles and-their-rims and-their-spokes and-their-hubs — all were cast.

**LOGOS (formal):** The wheels were made like a chariot wheel; their axles, their rims, their spokes, and their hubs were all cast.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The wheels were built like chariot wheels, with cast axles, rims, spokes, and hubs.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 35
**EMET (literal):** And-on-the-top-of the-stand — half a-cubit in-height, round all-around — and-on the-top-of the-stand, its-stays and-its-panels were from-it.

**LOGOS (formal):** On the top of the stand there was a round band half a cubit high; and on the top of the stand its stays and its panels were of one piece with it.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** On the top of each stand was a circular band nine inches high. The stays and panels on top were cast as one piece.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 37
**EMET (literal):** Like-this he-made ʾet-the-ten stands — one casting, one measure, one form for-all-of-them.

**LOGOS (formal):** After this manner he made the ten stands. All of them were cast alike, of the same measure and the same form.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** This is how he made all ten stands — each one identical in casting, size, and shape.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 38
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made ten basins-of bronze — forty baths each basin held. Four cubits was each basin. One basin was on each stand, for-the-ten stands.

**LOGOS (formal):** He made ten basins of bronze. Each basin held forty baths, each basin measured four cubits, and there was a basin for each of the ten stands.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He then made ten bronze basins, each holding about 240 gallons, each six feet across — one basin for each of the ten stands.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 41
**EMET (literal):** the-two pillars and-the-bowls-of the-capitals that were on-the-top-of the-two pillars, and-the-two networks to-cover ʾet-the-two bowls-of the-capitals that were on-the-top-of the-pillars,

**LOGOS (formal):** the two pillars, the two bowls of the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars, and the two latticeworks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the tops of the pillars,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of network covering the capitals;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 42
**EMET (literal):** and-the-four-hundred pomegranates for-the-two networks — two rows-of pomegranates for-the-one network — to-cover ʾet-the-two bowls-of the-capitals that were upon the-face-of the-pillars,

**LOGOS (formal):** and the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks — two rows of pomegranates for each network, covering the bowl-shaped capitals;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 43
**EMET (literal):** and-the-ten stands and-the-ten basins upon the-stands,

**LOGOS (formal):** the ten stands and the ten basins on the stands,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the ten stands with their ten basins;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 44
**EMET (literal):** and-the-one Sea and-the-twelve oxen beneath the-Sea,

**LOGOS (formal):** and the one sea and the twelve oxen under the sea,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the Sea with its twelve bulls underneath;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 47
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon left all the-vessels unweighed, because-of the-very great multitude — the-weight-of the-bronze was-not searched-out.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because there were so many of them; the weight of the bronze was not determined.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon did not weigh any of these items because there were so many — the total weight of the bronze was beyond calculation.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 48
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon made all the-vessels that were in-the-house-of YHWH: the-altar-of gold, and-the-table upon which was the-bread-of the-Presence — of-gold,

**LOGOS (formal):** So Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of the LORD: the golden altar, the golden table for the bread of the Presence,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon also made all the furnishings for the LORD's temple: the gold altar; the gold table for the bread of the Presence;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 49
**EMET (literal):** and-the-lampstands — five on-the-right and-five on-the-left before the-inner-sanctuary — of-refined gold, and-the-flowers and-the-lamps and-the-tongs — of-gold,

**LOGOS (formal):** the lampstands of pure gold, five on the south side and five on the north, before the inner sanctuary; the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of gold;

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the lampstands of pure gold — five on the right and five on the left in front of the inner sanctuary — with their gold flowers, lamps, and tongs;

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 50
**EMET (literal):** and-the-cups and-the-snuffers and-the-bowls and-the-spoons and-the-firepans — of-refined gold, and-the-hinges for-the-doors-of the-inner house, the-Holy-of-Holies, and-for-the-doors-of the-house, the-temple — of-gold.

**LOGOS (formal):** the cups, snuffers, basins, dishes for incense, and firepans, of pure gold; and the sockets of gold, for the doors of the innermost part of the house, the Most Holy Place, and for the doors of the nave of the temple.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** the pure gold cups, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, ladles, and censers; and the gold hinges for the doors of the inner sanctuary (the Most Holy Place) and for the doors of the main hall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
